title: The Raffle (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan warm baritone male vocal observational true story school raffle childhood Perth
lyrics:
[Intro - piano bar, expectant, warm]
Year four.
A school raffle.
Six thousand and five hundred dollars of prizes.
Midland brick paving.
You name it.
They got it all.

[Verse 1]
The school held a raffle
The way schools do
Everybody sells tickets
Everybody hopes it's them
They called first prize
Joel walked up
They called second prize
Corey walked up
And the room was maybe a little quiet
At that point
But they called third prize
And one of the McIvor boys walked up again
And the room went
Very quiet indeed

[Verse 2]
No one clapped for third
Not one person
Not a hand
Not a polite soft noise
Just the particular silence
Of people who have worked out
That the odds don't run like this
And have decided
That someone must have done something
To explain it

[Chorus]
The raffle
First, second, third
The raffle
Midland brick paving
You name it, they got it all
The raffle
Nobody clapped when they got the third
The raffle
The odds were not in their favour
That is what happened
The raffle
Sometimes winning
Is the loneliest thing
In the room

[Bridge - spoken, level, no bitterness]
They didn't do anything.
The tickets went in.
The tickets came out.
That's a raffle.
No one had to explain the mechanism.
Everyone understood the mechanism.
The silence was about something else entirely.
Year four.
Corey has thought about it a few times since.
The bricks were very good bricks.

[Chorus reprise]
The raffle
First, second, third
The raffle
Six thousand and five hundred dollars
The raffle
Joel and Corey walked up three times
The raffle
And the room remembered it
Long after the bricks were laid

[Outro - piano alone, dry and warm]
Chas was probably there
Watching
The way a father watches
When his boys are doing well
And the room decides
How to feel about that
The bricks went in the driveway
They're still there
